newsitem.title: UK: British Telecom rises on Labour comments.
newsitem.headline: British Telecom rises on Labour comments.

text.p: Shares in British Telecommunications Plc extended their gains at midday on Friday after the Labour Party said it would relax restrictions on telephone companies, dealers and analysts said.
By 1115 GMT, BT shares were up 7p to 499-1/2.
Shares in Cable and Wireless Plc, meanwhile, slipped one penny to 493-1/2.
The Labour Party, well placed to win the May 1 election, said it would reform Britain's competition laws early in the life of a new government.
The party said in its business manifesto that from 1998 it would progressively lift restrictions on the freedom of telephone to offer entertainment services over their networks nLBT4945.

"This means that BT could potentially broadcast entertainment over telephone lines and compete with the cable companies," said one analyst. "We need more details, but this is not a good story for Cable and Wireless."
Although there are current restrictions on Cable and Wireless' ability to offer broadcast services, these were relaxed last year when its UK operation, Mercury, received a new licence.

However, some analysts said the strength of BT's share price may be due to index-linked funds buying the stock ahead of the company's planned merger with MCI Communications Corp, which will create one of the biggest stocks in the FTSE 100.
Dealers said the market for BT shares had been firm ahead of Labour's comments after SocGen and SBC Warburg on Thursday reiterated their "buy" ratings.
